sentences.text: Shri B.N.Malhotra- Advocate for respondent/Insurance C  ORDER

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant-Ram Prasad, claiming to be the legal heir of deceased Smt. Sukhiya Bai (original claimant), challenging the award dated 24.03.2005 passed by Second Additional Member to the Court of First Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Guna (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 38/2004, whereby the claim petition has been dismissed.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Guna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The date of accident, the issue of negligence, and the liability of the offending vehicle are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the learned Tribunal committed grave illegality in dismissing the claim petition without proper appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence on record and in disregard NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4506 2 MA-883-2005 of the settled principles of law.

It was further submitted that after the death of the original claimant,
Smt. Sukhiya Bai, during the pendency of the claim petition, the appellant Ram Prasad, being the beneficiary and representative of her estate under a Will, was rightly brought on record as her legal heir and no objection was raised by the respondents to such substitution.
It was argued that Sukhiya Bai[D] Pannalal[D] Lrs Ram Pd. vs Balbeer Singh And Ors.

sentences.text: On these grounds, prayer was made for setting aside the impugned award.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the appeal lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
6.
Upon careful consideration of the material available on record, it is evident that the appellant failed to prove the execution and validity of the alleged Will.
Further, the appellant was also unable to establish that he was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4506 3 MA-883-2005 adopted by the deceased Sukhiya Bai in accordance with law.
In absence of proof of the Will as well as adoption, the appellant could not establish his status as a legal representative/dependent entitled to claim compensation.

7. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court finds that the Claims Tribunal has rightly held that the appellant was not entitled to receive compensation and has rightly dismissed the claim petition.
8. This Court finds no perversity, illegality, or infirmity in the impugned award warranting interference in exercise of appellate jurisdiction.
The miscellaneous appeal, being devoid of merit, is accordingly dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
